text:
TREC’s 2025 Product Recommendation task provides the closest annotation template: functional substitutes, complements, unrelated items, and “unable to assess.” Crucially, it distinguishes complementary products with unknown compatibility from documented incompatibility. This supports separate relation and compatibility labels; missing specifications should trigger uncertainty, never an incompatibility claim. Functional substitution alone also does not establish unwanted redundancy: replacement, collection, or exploration intent may be unobserved. [Official annotation guidelines](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html).

Annotation reliability needs explicit checks. ALERT (NAACL 2025) decomposes recommendation-explanation judgments into subquestions with examples, but reports expert inter-annotator Krippendorff’s α=0.24—substantial uncertainty despite structured instructions. SCREEN (2024) uses three annotators and reports Fleiss’s κ around 0.4–0.6. These findings support piloting definitions, independently double-annotating cases, reporting agreement separately for each dimension, and retaining disagreements and abstentions before adjudication. [ALERT](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.137.pdf), [SCREEN](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=BfjHOCFvyf).

Proposed adaptation: each judgment records the recommended item, relevant history item(s), quoted title/description evidence, timestamps, relation, compatibility, possible redundancy, temporal support, and an explicit insufficient-evidence option. Require evidence for each affirmative label; an old interaction alone cannot establish an outdated interest. Report label counts, assessable-case denominators, abstention rates, agreement, and illustrative disagreements for the twenty training users, separated by category. Treat these as descriptive audits of observable recommendation properties, not representative preference ground truth. Keep the fixed macro validation HR@10 selection criterion: the 2025 sequential-evaluation study shows that evaluation choices can change scores and model rankings. [Time to Split](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748164).
